entries.title: Hunting Shots
entries.body:
# Hunting Shots

## Overview
The greatest Rangers are not defined by the weapons they carry, but by the techniques they master. Hunting Shots represent years of specialised training, allowing a Ranger to perform extraordinary feats of marksmanship beyond a standard attack.

Upon learning this talent, the Ranger unlocks their first Hunting Shot and first Trick Shot. Hunting Shots are specialised combat techniques designed to control or weaken enemies, while Trick Shots demonstrate exceptional skill, allowing impossible angles and creative solutions both in and out of combat.

As the Ranger grows stronger, additional ranks unlock new shots rather than replacing old ones, creating an ever-expanding arsenal of precision techniques.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The greatest Rangers are not defined by the weapons they carry, but by the techniques they master. Hunting Shots represent years of specialised training, allowing a Ranger to perform extraordinary feats of marksmanship beyond a standard attack.

Upon learning this talent, the Ranger unlocks their first Hunting Shot and first Trick Shot. Hunting Shots are specialised combat techniques designed to control or weaken enemies, while Trick Shots demonstrate exceptional skill, allowing impossible angles and creative solutions both in and out of combat.

As the Ranger grows stronger, additional ranks unlock new shots rather than replacing old ones, creating an ever-expanding arsenal of precision techniques.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Stunning Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 15 SP

After making a successful ranged weapon attack, you may declare it as a **Stunning Shot**.

- The target must succeed on a **Constitution Saving Throw**.
- On a failure, the target becomes **Staggered** until the end of its next turn.
- While Staggered, the target cannot take Reactions and has Disadvantage on its next attack roll.
- On a successful save, the target suffers normal weapon damage with no additional effect.

#### Trick Shot — Curve Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 10 SP

The Ranger applies exceptional spin and trajectory to a projectile.

- Fire around corners, trees, pillars, or similar obstacles.
- Ignore partial line-of-sight restrictions where a curved trajectory is physically possible.
- Reduce penalties for difficult or unconventional ranged attacks, at the GM's discretion.
- This shot cannot pass through solid objects or total cover.

#### General Rules

- Only one Hunting Shot or Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Additional Hunting Shots and Trick Shots are unlocked by increasing this talent's rank.

---

### Lore

Every Ranger Lodge teaches that an arrow is only as effective as the mind guiding it. While ordinary archers rely upon accuracy alone, Rangers develop specialised techniques that allow each shot to serve a unique purpose. Whether disabling prey, striking impossible angles, or controlling the battlefield, every technique reflects countless hours of disciplined practice.

Veteran Rangers often recognise one another not by the bows they carry, but by the techniques they employ. Many legendary Hunting Shots have been passed from mentor to apprentice for centuries, with each generation refining and expanding the art of precision marksmanship.

---

> *"Any archer can loose an arrow. A Ranger chooses exactly what that arrow will accomplish."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

As the Ranger's mastery grows, so too does their arsenal of specialised techniques. Every hunt presents new challenges, and experienced Rangers learn that a single type of shot cannot solve every problem. Through relentless practice, they develop new methods capable of overcoming heavily armoured prey and striking enemies from angles they believe to be impossible.

At this rank, the Ranger unlocks two new techniques: **Drill Shot**, a devastating armour-piercing attack designed to punch through resilient defences, and **Ricochet Shot**, a trick shot that uses hard surfaces to strike targets from unexpected directions. These techniques reward creativity, positioning, and battlefield awareness.

A skilled Ranger is never limited by a straight line. They learn to make every obstacle another tool in their hunt.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Drill Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 20 SP

The Ranger fires a specialised armour-piercing projectile designed to bore through armour, scales, and hardened hides.

- Make a ranged weapon attack as normal.
- On a successful hit, the attack **ignores Half Cover**.
- The attack ignores **2 points of Armour Rating or Natural Armour** (or an equivalent value determined by the GM).
- Drill Shot may only affect the initial target and cannot strike additional creatures.

#### Trick Shot — Ricochet Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 15 SP

The Ranger deliberately bounces a projectile off a hard surface before striking the intended target.

- The projectile may ricochet off one solid surface before hitting its target.
- The shot may ignore obstacles that would normally block a direct line of fire, provided a reasonable ricochet path exists.
- Reduce penalties for indirect shots at the GM's discretion.
- Ricochet Shot cannot pass through solid objects or total cover.

#### General Rules

- The Ranger retains access to **Stunning Shot** and **Curve Shot**.
- Only one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Additional Hunting Shots and Trick Shots are unlocked by increasing this talent's rank.

---

### Lore

Among Ranger Lodges, the second rank of Hunting Shots marks the point where an apprentice begins to think beyond conventional marksmanship. Rather than simply aiming at a target, they learn to manipulate both the projectile and the environment, turning armour into a weakness and obstacles into opportunities.

Many famous Rangers earned their reputations through shots that others believed impossible. Tales speak of arrows skipping from stone walls, bolts punching through thick scales, and hunters striking prey that never even realised they had been exposed. Such techniques are only possible through unwavering discipline and countless hours of practice.

---

> *"When the path is blocked, do not change your target—change the path."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger has progressed beyond mastering individual techniques and now learns to manipulate both the battlefield and the enemy's movements. Every shot is carefully chosen to restrict, outmanoeuvre, or overwhelm their quarry before the decisive strike is delivered.

At this rank, the Ranger unlocks **Pinning Shot**, a technique designed to hinder an opponent's movement, and **Split Shot**, a remarkable feat of precision that allows a single attack to threaten multiple targets. These techniques showcase the Ranger's growing mastery over both control and precision.

Veteran Rangers know that victory is often determined long before the final arrow is loosed. By controlling where an enemy can move and how they react, the hunt becomes all but inevitable.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Pinning Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 25 SP

The Ranger fires a carefully placed shot intended to restrict the target's movement rather than inflict maximum injury.

- Make a ranged weapon attack as normal.
- On a successful hit, the target must succeed on a **Strength Saving Throw** or become **Pinned** until the end of its next turn.
- While Pinned:
  - The target's movement speed is reduced to **0**.
  - The target cannot Dash.
- Flying creatures that fail the saving throw immediately descend safely to the ground if able, or have their flying speed reduced to 0 until the effect ends (GM discretion).
- Creatures that are significantly larger than the projectile may gain Advantage on the saving throw.

#### Trick Shot — Split Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 20 SP

The Ranger performs an extraordinary feat of marksmanship, releasing two projectiles almost simultaneously.

- Make one attack roll against two creatures within **3 metres** of each other.
- Compare the same attack roll against each target's Armour Class.
- Roll damage separately for each creature that is successfully hit.
- Ammunition for both shots is still consumed.

#### General Rules

- The Ranger retains access to **Stunning Shot**, **Curve Shot**, **Drill Shot**, and **Ricochet Shot**.
- Only one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Additional Hunting Shots and Trick Shots are unlocked by increasing this talent's rank.

---

### Lore

By the third rank, a Ranger's techniques become recognised throughout the Lodges as the mark of a seasoned hunter. They no longer rely solely on accuracy but instead shape the flow of battle itself, deciding where prey may run and when it must stand its ground.

Stories speak of master Rangers pinning charging beasts to ancient trees before turning a single fluid movement into two perfectly placed arrows that felled separate enemies. Such feats are impossible without years of disciplined practice, unwavering focus, and complete trust in one's own skill.

---

> *"A true hunter does not simply strike their prey—they decide where it may stand, where it may run, and when the hunt shall end."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

Master Rangers understand that a well-placed arrow can control the battlefield just as effectively as it can wound an enemy. By the fourth rank, they have developed techniques capable of overwhelming even the largest foes, using raw impact and exceptional skill to dictate the flow of combat.

At this rank, the Ranger unlocks **Impact Shot**, a devastating attack that uses tremendous force to drive enemies backwards or knock them from their feet, and **Arcing Shot**, a specialised technique that allows projectiles to travel in a high trajectory, striking enemies hiding behind walls, fortifications, or other obstacles.

These techniques demonstrate that a master Ranger is not limited by distance, cover, or terrain. Every obstacle becomes another opportunity to land the perfect shot.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Impact Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 30 SP

The Ranger delivers a powerful shot designed to overwhelm the target through sheer force.

- Make a ranged weapon attack as normal.
- On a successful hit, the target must succeed on a **Strength Saving Throw**.
- On a failed save:
  - The target is pushed **3 metres** directly away from the Ranger.
  - If the target cannot be pushed because it collides with a solid object, it is instead **knocked Prone**.
- On a successful save, the target suffers normal weapon damage but is not pushed or knocked prone.
- **Large** creatures have **Advantage** on the saving throw.
- **Huge** and larger creatures cannot be pushed but may still be knocked **Prone** at the GM's discretion.

#### Trick Shot — Arcing Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 20 SP

The Ranger launches a projectile in a high, controlled arc to strike targets beyond conventional lines of fire.

- Ignore obstacles that block a direct shot provided a clear aerial trajectory exists.
- You may target creatures behind low walls, battlements, trenches, or similar cover.
- The target does not benefit from **Half Cover** provided the arc successfully bypasses it.
- The GM determines whether sufficient overhead clearance exists for the shot.

#### General Rules

- The Ranger retains access to all previously unlocked Hunting Shots and Trick Shots.
- Only one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Additional Hunting Shots and Trick Shots are unlocked by increasing this talent's rank.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, the fourth rank of Hunting Shots is considered the mark of a battlefield master. These Rangers no longer think only about defeating a single opponent—they shape the entire battlefield, forcing enemies into vulnerable positions while striking those who believed themselves safely protected.

Many military commanders have sought the aid of master Rangers during sieges and large-scale battles. Their ability to strike defenders behind walls, scatter charging enemies, and manipulate the flow of combat has turned the tide of countless conflicts throughout Asteria.

---

> *"A wall is only protection until a Ranger learns to shoot over it. Strength is only an advantage until a Ranger learns to throw you backwards."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has reached the pinnacle of ranged weapon mastery. Every arrow, bolt, bullet, or thrown projectile becomes an extension of their will, capable of travelling extraordinary distances and striking with impossible precision. No battlefield is too large, no target too distant, and no obstacle too daunting for a true master of Hunting Shots.

At this rank, the Ranger unlocks **Horizon Shot**, a legendary technique that dramatically extends the effective range of their ranged weapon, allowing them to engage enemies long before those enemies can retaliate. Alongside it, the Ranger also masters **Impossible Shot**, a technique reserved for only the greatest marksmen, capable of accomplishing feats that most would consider beyond belief.

Among the Ranger Lodges, only a handful of hunters throughout history have ever demonstrated these techniques in battle. Their shots are remembered for generations, becoming stories told around campfires as examples of what true dedication can achieve.

---

### Effects

#### Hunting Shot — Horizon Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 35 SP

The Ranger unleashes a perfectly calculated shot designed to travel far beyond the normal limits of their weapon.

- Increase the weapon's **maximum range by 50%** for this attack.
- Ignore penalties associated with attacking at **long range**.
- The attack ignores **Half Cover**.
- Horizon Shot may be used with any ranged weapon.

#### Trick Shot — Impossible Shot

**Stamina Cost:** 25 SP

The Ranger performs a feat of marksmanship bordering on legend.

Choose one of the following when making the attack:

- Thread a projectile through an exceptionally narrow opening.
- Strike a tiny unattended object.
- Cut a rope, chain, or similar object.
- Trigger a distant mechanism.
- Perform another extraordinary ranged feat, subject to GM approval.

The GM may reduce or remove penalties for exceptionally difficult shots when Impossible Shot is used.

#### General Rules

- The Ranger retains access to every previously unlocked Hunting Shot and Trick Shot.
- Only one Hunting Shot or one Trick Shot may be applied to a single attack unless another ability states otherwise.
- Hunting Shots may only be used with ranged weapons.
- Impossible Shot cannot bypass magical barriers or ignore total cover.

---

### Lore

The fifth rank of Hunting Shots is spoken of with near-mythical reverence throughout the Ranger Lodges. Tales tell of Rangers striking enemy commanders from across entire valleys, severing bridge supports with a single arrow, or saving companions by cutting ropes and triggering mechanisms at precisely the right moment.

These feats are not considered luck or magic—they are the culmination of decades of unwavering discipline, flawless technique, and an intimate understanding of both weapon and environment. To witness a master Ranger employ Horizon Shot or Impossible Shot is to witness the very peak of mortal marksmanship.

---

> *"Distance is an obstacle only to those who doubt their aim."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, Master Marksman of the Emerald Lodge**

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

entries.title: Predator's Roar
entries.body:
# Predator's Roar

## Overview
The wilderness belongs to those who command respect, not through words, but through presence alone. Predator's Roar allows the Ranger to unleash a thunderous battle cry that echoes the dominance of the world's greatest hunters. It is not magic, but the culmination of unwavering confidence, survival instinct, and countless victories over dangerous prey.

When the Ranger roars, nearby allies are reminded that they stand beside a seasoned hunter, while enemies instinctively recognise the arrival of a predator. Even creatures that have never encountered the Ranger may hesitate for a brief moment as instinct tells them they have become the prey.

Though its effects are subtle at first, Predator's Roar becomes increasingly terrifying as the Ranger's reputation and mastery grow.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The wilderness belongs to those who command respect, not through words, but through presence alone. Predator's Roar allows the Ranger to unleash a thunderous battle cry that echoes the dominance of the world's greatest hunters. It is not magic, but the culmination of unwavering confidence, survival instinct, and countless victories over dangerous prey.

When the Ranger roars, nearby allies are reminded that they stand beside a seasoned hunter, while enemies instinctively recognise the arrival of a predator. Even creatures that have never encountered the Ranger may hesitate for a brief moment as instinct tells them they have become the prey.

Though its effects are subtle at first, Predator's Roar becomes increasingly terrifying as the Ranger's reputation and mastery grow.

---

### Effects

#### Predator's Roar

**Cost:** 30 SP

Unleash a powerful roar affecting all creatures within **10 metres**.

**Enemies**

- Creatures of your choice must make a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- On a failure, they become **Shaken** until the end of their next turn.
- While Shaken:
  - They have **Disadvantage on their first attack roll**.
  - They cannot take **Reactions** until the start of their next turn.
- On a successful save, the creature is unaffected.

**Allies**

Friendly creatures within range gain:

- **+1 Morale Bonus** to their next attack roll before the end of their next turn.
- Immunity to the **Shaken** condition caused by your Predator's Roar.

#### Limitations

- Predator's Roar does not affect creatures that cannot hear you.
- A creature can only be affected by your Predator's Roar once per use.
- This is a non-magical ability and may affect creatures normally immune to magical fear, subject to GM discretion.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, Predator's Roar is taught only after a hunter has proven themselves against formidable prey. It is said that every great predator possesses a presence capable of unsettling even the strongest opponent before the hunt has truly begun.

Legends speak of Rangers whose roars halted charging beasts, scattered packs of wolves, and emboldened exhausted companions to fight on. While many dismiss these stories as exaggeration, those who have stood beside a master Ranger know that confidence itself can become a weapon.

To the Ranger, the roar is not a challenge—it is a declaration that the hunt has already begun, and that every creature who hears it has a choice: stand and fight, or flee.

---

> *"The loudest roar is not the one born of anger—it is the one that reminds the forest who sits at the top of the food chain."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's roar carries far greater authority, echoing with the confidence of a hunter that has survived countless battles. It is no longer simply a display of dominance—it becomes an instinctive declaration that the Ranger has claimed the battlefield as their hunting ground.

Those who hear the roar often react before they even realise why. Allies stand taller, emboldened by the presence of an experienced hunter, while enemies hesitate as primal instincts warn them that they have become the prey. Even disciplined warriors can find themselves momentarily shaken by the sheer conviction behind the Ranger's voice.

Among the Ranger Lodges, this level of mastery is often called the **Call of the Alpha**, symbolising a hunter whose presence alone begins to influence the outcome of the battle.

---

### Effects

#### Predator's Roar

**Cost:** 35 SP

Unleash a powerful roar affecting all creatures of your choice within **12 metres**.

**Enemies**

- Creatures must succeed on a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- On a failure, they become **Shaken** until the end of their next turn.
- While Shaken:
  - They have **Disadvantage on their first attack roll**.
  - They cannot take **Reactions** until the start of their next turn.
  - Their movement speed is reduced by **3 metres** until the end of their next turn.
- On a successful save, the creature is unaffected.

**Allies**

Friendly creatures within range gain:

- **+2 Morale Bonus** to their next attack roll.
- **+2 Morale Bonus** to their next Wisdom Saving Throw against **Fear** or **Charm** effects.
- Immunity to the **Shaken** condition caused by your Predator's Roar.

#### Limitations

- Predator's Roar does not affect creatures that cannot hear you.
- A creature may only be affected once each time you use Predator's Roar.
- This is a non-magical ability and does not count as a fear spell or magical effect.

---

### Lore

As Rangers continue to master Predator's Roar, they begin to understand that true dominance is communicated long before weapons are drawn. A confident stance, unwavering composure, and a commanding roar are often enough to make predators reconsider the hunt and force hostile creatures into moments of hesitation.

Veteran Rangers are known for leading hunting parties through little more than their presence. Companions speak of feeling an overwhelming sense of confidence the moment the roar echoes through the wilderness, while enemies often remember it as the sound that marked the beginning of their defeat.

Within the Lodges, apprentices are taught that a roar should never be wasted. Every use is a declaration that the Ranger intends to control the battlefield from that moment forward.

---

> *"The strongest predator does not roar because it is angry. It roars because it already knows who will survive the hunt."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger's roar now carries the authority of an apex predator. It resonates across the battlefield with such conviction that even seasoned warriors instinctively hesitate, while allies rally behind the certainty of a proven hunter. The roar no longer serves merely as intimidation—it establishes the Ranger as the dominant force in the encounter.

At this level, the Ranger has learned to channel every hard-earned victory, every dangerous hunt, and every brush with death into a single commanding cry. Those who stand beside the Ranger find renewed courage, while enemies begin to question whether they are the hunter or the hunted.

Among the Ranger Lodges, achieving the third rank is regarded as the point where a Ranger no longer survives the wilderness—they command it.

---

### Effects

#### Predator's Roar

**Cost:** 40 SP

Unleash a commanding roar affecting all creatures of your choice within **15 metres**.

**Enemies**

- Creatures must succeed on a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- On a failed save, they become **Shaken** until the end of their next turn.
- While Shaken:
  - They have **Disadvantage on all attack rolls** until the end of their next turn.
  - They cannot take **Reactions**.
  - Their movement speed is reduced by **6 metres**.
- On a successful save, the creature is unaffected.

**Allies**

Friendly creatures within range gain:

- **+2 Morale Bonus** to attack rolls for **1 minute**.
- **+2 Morale Bonus** to Wisdom Saving Throws against **Fear** and **Charm** effects.
- Immunity to the **Shaken** condition caused by your Predator's Roar while the effect lasts.

#### Limitations

- Predator's Roar does not affect creatures that cannot hear you.
- A creature can only be affected once each time Predator's Roar is used.
- This is a non-magical ability and is not considered a magical fear effect.

---

### Lore

Only respected Rangers earn the right to teach the third rank of Predator's Roar. Their voices become symbols of confidence, discipline, and unwavering resolve, carrying across forests, mountains, and battlefields alike. Veteran adventurers often speak of the calm that settles over them when they hear such a roar, knowing an experienced hunter now leads the fight.

Wild beasts react instinctively to this display of dominance. Lesser predators retreat, territorial creatures hesitate, and even intelligent foes recognise the confidence of someone who has faced death countless times and prevailed. Within the Ranger Lodges, this technique is often described as the moment a hunter truly becomes the alpha.

---

> *"The forest does not choose its apex predator by strength alone. It chooses the one whose presence makes every other creature stop and listen."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's roar has become the unmistakable call of an apex predator. It echoes across the battlefield with overwhelming authority, disrupting enemy morale while rallying companions to fight with renewed determination. Few creatures can ignore the instinctive warning carried within its thunderous cry.

Years of surviving impossible hunts have forged the Ranger into a symbol of confidence and dominance. Every roar reminds allies why they chose to follow, while enemies begin to realise they are no longer fighting a lone warrior—they are facing the leader of the hunt.

Among the Ranger Lodges, reaching this level is considered the mark of a Hunt Leader, someone capable of directing an entire party through presence alone.

---

### Effects

#### Predator's Roar

**Cost:** 45 SP

Unleash a terrifying roar affecting all creatures of your choice within **18 metres**.

**Enemies**

- Creatures must succeed on a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- On a failed save, they become **Shaken** for **1 minute**.
- Affected creatures may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.
- While Shaken:
  - They have **Disadvantage on all attack rolls**.
  - They cannot take **Reactions**.
  - Their movement speed is reduced by **6 metres**.
  - They have **Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks** made to locate or detect the Ranger.

**Allies**

Friendly creatures within range gain:

- **+3 Morale Bonus** to attack rolls.
- **+3 Morale Bonus** to Wisdom Saving Throws against **Fear** and **Charm** effects.
- Immunity to the **Shaken** condition caused by your Predator's Roar.
- Advantage on **Initiative rolls** if combat begins immediately after using Predator's Roar, at the GM's discretion.

#### Limitations

- Predator's Roar does not affect creatures that cannot hear you.
- A creature may only be affected once per use of Predator's Roar.
- This is a non-magical ability and is not considered a magical fear effect.
- Creatures immune to being frightened are not automatically immune to **Shaken**; the GM determines whether instinctive intimidation still affects them.

---

### Lore

Only the most respected Rangers ever master the fourth rank of Predator's Roar. Their voice carries the confidence of countless successful hunts, becoming a symbol recognised throughout Asteria. Entire hunting parties have been known to rally behind a single roar, while enemy formations falter before the battle has truly begun.

The oldest Ranger texts describe this technique as **The Call of the Apex**, teaching that dominance is earned through survival, patience, and mastery rather than brute strength. When such a roar echoes across the wilderness, every creature understands that the hunt now belongs to the Ranger.

---

> *"The wise flee from the roar. The foolish answer it. Either way, the hunt has already begun."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has become the embodiment of an apex predator. Their roar is more than a battle cry—it is an instinctive declaration of absolute dominance that echoes across the battlefield. Allies are inspired to fight with unmatched confidence, while enemies instinctively recognise they have become the hunted.

At this level, Predator's Roar carries the weight of countless victories and years spent surviving against creatures far stronger than oneself. Even disciplined soldiers and legendary beasts hesitate for a fleeting moment as ancient instincts tell them they stand before a hunter who has never abandoned a pursuit.

Within the Ranger Lodges, mastering Predator's Roar is one of the highest honours a hunter can achieve. Those who hear it know the hunt has already begun, and those who stand beside the Ranger know they are following the leader of the pack.

---

### Effects

#### Predator's Roar

**Cost:** 50 SP

Unleash a terrifying roar affecting all creatures of your choice within **20 metres**.

**Enemies**

- Creatures must succeed on a **Wisdom Saving Throw**.
- On a failed save, they become **Shaken** for **1 minute**.
- Affected creatures may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.
- While Shaken:
  - They have **Disadvantage on all attack rolls**.
  - They cannot take **Reactions**.
  - Their movement speed is reduced by **6 metres**.
  - They have **Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception)** checks made to detect or locate the Ranger.
  - They have **Disadvantage on saving throws** against the Ranger's Hunting Shots.

**Allies**

Friendly creatures within range gain:

- **+4 Morale Bonus** to attack rolls.
- **+4 Morale Bonus** to Wisdom Saving Throws against **Fear** and **Charm** effects.
- Immunity to the **Shaken** condition caused by your Predator's Roar.
- **Advantage on Initiative rolls** if combat begins before the end of your next turn.
- The first successful attack each ally makes before the end of their next turn deals **+1d4 bonus damage**.

#### Limitations

- Predator's Roar does not affect creatures that cannot hear you.
- A creature may only be affected once each time Predator's Roar is used.
- This is a non-magical ability and is not considered a magical fear effect.
- Creatures immune to magical fear are not automatically immune to Predator's Roar, as it represents instinctive intimidation rather than supernatural influence. The GM has final discretion.

---

### Lore

Only a handful of Rangers throughout history have mastered the fifth rank of Predator's Roar. Their names are remembered not only for the monsters they slew, but for the unwavering confidence they inspired in every companion who fought beside them. Entire hunting parties have rallied behind a single roar, turning hopeless battles into legendary victories.

The oldest Ranger traditions teach that every forest, mountain, and wilderness has an apex predator whose presence alone commands respect. Those who master Predator's Roar become the mortal embodiment of that principle. Their roar carries no magic, only the certainty born from countless successful hunts. To friend and foe alike, it is the unmistakable sound of the hunt reaching its inevitable conclusion.

---

> *"The greatest predator does not prove its strength with its claws. It proves it with the silence that follows its roar."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**

## Prerequisites
None

See individual rank details.

entries.title: Survival Instinct
entries.body:
# Survival Instinct

## Overview
Years spent surviving in the untamed wilderness have sharpened the Ranger's instincts beyond those of ordinary adventurers. Constant exposure to predators, harsh environments, and unexpected dangers has taught them to recognise subtle signs of trouble long before others become aware of them.

Survival Instinct is not a learned technique, but a collection of natural reactions developed through experience. A snapped twig, an unnatural silence among wildlife, or the faint scent of smoke is often enough to place the Ranger on alert. While others rely on preparation, the Ranger trusts instinct.

This heightened awareness allows the Ranger to react more quickly to danger, avoid natural hazards, and survive in environments that would overwhelm less experienced travellers.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

Years spent surviving in the untamed wilderness have sharpened the Ranger's instincts beyond those of ordinary adventurers. Constant exposure to predators, harsh environments, and unexpected dangers has taught them to recognise subtle signs of trouble long before others become aware of them.

Survival Instinct is not a learned technique, but a collection of natural reactions developed through experience. A snapped twig, an unnatural silence among wildlife, or the faint scent of smoke is often enough to place the Ranger on alert. While others rely on preparation, the Ranger trusts instinct.

This heightened awareness allows the Ranger to react more quickly to danger, avoid natural hazards, and survive in environments that would overwhelm less experienced travellers.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+2** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+2** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including quicksand, unstable ground, rockfalls, thin ice, poisonous plants, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+2** to detect **ambushes** or hidden creatures before combat begins.
- Gain **+2** to resist becoming **Lost** while travelling through natural environments.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **twice the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require **half the normal time** to establish a safe campsite or shelter in the wilderness.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, Survival Instinct is considered one of the first signs that a hunter has truly embraced the wilderness. It cannot be taught through books or drills alone. Instead, it is forged through countless nights beneath the open sky, surviving storms, avoiding predators, and learning to read the world as though it were a living companion.

Veteran Rangers often claim they cannot explain how they know danger is near—they simply do. Whether it is the sudden silence of birds, the shift of the wind, or an almost imperceptible feeling that something is wrong, these instincts have saved countless lives throughout Asteria.

To the untrained eye, it appears to be luck. To a Ranger, it is simply experience speaking louder than words.

---

> *"The wilderness whispers before it strikes. A Ranger survives because they learned to listen."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's instincts continue to sharpen, becoming second nature after countless journeys through dangerous wilderness. They no longer simply recognise danger—they begin anticipating it before it fully reveals itself. Subtle changes in weather, wildlife behaviour, or the environment immediately draw the Ranger's attention.

Experience has also taught the Ranger to conserve energy and resources while travelling. They instinctively choose safer paths, identify reliable sources of food and water, and establish secure camps with remarkable efficiency. What would take others hours of careful planning becomes routine for a seasoned Ranger.

Among the Ranger Lodges, reaching this level is considered the point where a Ranger can confidently guide an expedition through even the most hostile regions of Asteria.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+4** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+4** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including quicksand, unstable ground, rockfalls, thin ice, poisonous plants, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+4** to detect **ambushes** or hidden creatures before combat begins.
- Gain **+4** to resist becoming **Lost** while travelling through natural environments.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **three times the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require **half the normal time** to establish a safe campsite or shelter.
- Gain **+2** to saving throws against **natural diseases and natural poisons**.

---

### Lore

Veteran Rangers often joke that the wilderness itself begins to guide those who survive long enough. While outsiders dismiss this as superstition, experienced hunters know that years spent living among nature cultivate instincts that cannot be learned from books or training grounds.

Many expeditions owe their survival to a Ranger noticing the smallest warning signs—a sudden change in birdsong, fresh claw marks on a tree, or the scent of rain carried by the wind. Such observations often mean the difference between arriving safely and walking into disaster.

Within the Lodges, Rangers of this rank are frequently entrusted with leading scouting parties and long-distance expeditions, for their instincts have proven reliable time and time again.

---

> *"Maps show where the road was. Instinct tells you where it should never go."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger's survival instincts have become an inseparable part of who they are. Every sense is constantly evaluating the world around them, allowing them to react to danger with remarkable speed and confidence. Their experience enables them to notice threats long before they become obvious, often avoiding danger altogether rather than simply surviving it.

By this stage, the Ranger has learned to thrive in environments that would overwhelm most travellers. Whether crossing frozen tundras, scorching deserts, dense forests, or towering mountain ranges, they instinctively adapt to changing conditions while guiding both themselves and their companions safely through the wilderness.

Among the Ranger Lodges, this level of mastery earns the title of **Pathfinder**, recognising those trusted to lead expeditions into the most dangerous regions of Asteria.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+6** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+6** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including unstable terrain, traps, rockfalls, thin ice, poisonous plants, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+6** to detect **ambushes** or hidden creatures before combat begins.
- Gain **+6** to resist becoming **Lost** while travelling through natural environments.
- Gain **+4** to saving throws against **natural diseases** and **natural poisons**.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **four times the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require only **one-quarter of the normal time** to establish a safe campsite or wilderness shelter.
- You and creatures travelling with you ignore **non-magical difficult terrain** while travelling outside of combat.

---

### Lore

Rangers who achieve the third rank of Survival Instinct become renowned throughout Asteria as guides capable of crossing regions that others consider impassable. Their understanding of the natural world extends far beyond tracking prey—they read the land itself, predicting dangers before they arise and finding safe passage where none appears to exist.

Many kingdoms employ such Rangers to escort caravans, military expeditions, and explorers into the unknown. Their reputation is built not upon the monsters they have slain, but upon the countless lives they have brought home safely.

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are taught that surviving the wilderness is no longer enough. A true Pathfinder ensures that everyone under their guidance survives as well.

---

> *"The wilderness is neither friend nor foe. It simply rewards those wise enough to understand it."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger's instincts now border on supernatural, though they remain entirely the product of experience, discipline, and countless years spent surviving where few others could. Every sound, scent, and subtle movement is unconsciously processed, allowing the Ranger to anticipate danger before it fully reveals itself.

No environment feels truly hostile anymore. Frozen tundras, scorching deserts, ancient forests, and monster-infested swamps become familiar territory where the Ranger can move with confidence. Their instincts extend beyond personal survival, allowing them to guide companions safely through the harshest regions of Asteria.

Within the Ranger Lodges, those who attain this rank are known as **Wayfinders**, trusted to lead expeditions into lands that have never before been explored.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+8** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+8** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including unstable terrain, hidden pitfalls, avalanches, poisonous flora, quicksand, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+8** to detect **ambushes**, hidden creatures, and concealed natural threats before combat begins.
- Gain **+8** to checks made to avoid becoming **Lost** in natural environments.
- Gain **+6** to saving throws against **natural diseases**, **natural poisons**, and **environmental hazards**.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **five times the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require only **one-quarter of the normal time** to establish a secure campsite or wilderness shelter.
- You and creatures travelling with you ignore **non-magical difficult terrain** while travelling and suffer no movement penalty from natural terrain outside of combat.
- You have **Advantage** on initiative rolls when combat begins as the result of a natural ambush or environmental encounter.

---

### Lore

Only the most accomplished Rangers ever achieve the fourth rank of Survival Instinct. Their reputation spreads far beyond the Ranger Lodges, and kings, merchants, and explorers alike seek their guidance before venturing into dangerous lands. Stories tell of Wayfinders leading entire expeditions across continents without losing a single traveller, avoiding disasters that others never even realised existed.

To these Rangers, survival is no longer about endurance—it is about understanding the wilderness as a living, ever-changing world. They read the wind like a map, recognise danger in the silence of birds, and instinctively choose the safest path long before others realise there was ever a choice.

---

> *"The greatest guide is not the one who knows every path. It is the one who always knows which path not to take."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has become one with the wilderness. Every sense operates in perfect harmony, constantly reading the environment without conscious thought. A subtle shift in the wind, the sudden silence of wildlife, or a barely visible footprint is enough for the Ranger to recognise danger long before it threatens them.

To a master Ranger, survival is no longer a skill—it is instinct. They move through the harshest regions of Asteria as though they were home, adapting effortlessly to changing conditions while guiding others with absolute confidence. Where others see an impassable wilderness, the Ranger sees opportunity, safety, and countless paths forward.

The greatest Rangers are said to possess an almost mythical awareness of their surroundings. Whether these stories are exaggerated or not, one truth remains unchanged: very few who travel beside a master Ranger fail to return home.

---

### Effects

- Gain **+10** to **Survival** skill checks.
- Gain **+10** to checks made to detect **natural hazards**, including unstable terrain, hidden sinkholes, avalanches, poisonous flora, quicksand, thin ice, and similar environmental dangers.
- Gain **+10** to detect **ambushes**, hidden creatures, concealed traps, and environmental threats before combat begins.
- Gain **+10** to checks made to avoid becoming **Lost** in natural environments.
- Gain **+8** to saving throws against **natural diseases**, **natural poisons**, and **environmental hazards**.
- You may forage for food and fresh water at **six times the normal rate**, subject to the GM's discretion.
- You require only **one-tenth of the normal time** to establish a secure campsite or wilderness shelter.
- You and creatures travelling with you ignore **all non-magical difficult terrain** while travelling.
- You have **Advantage** on Initiative rolls whenever combat begins due to an ambush or environmental encounter.
- Once per **Long Rest**, if you would be **Surprised**, you may ignore the **Surprised** condition.

---

### Lore

Only the legendary Huntmasters of Asteria ever reach the fifth rank of Survival Instinct. Their names become synonymous with exploration, endurance, and impossible journeys. They are the guides sought by kings venturing into forgotten ruins, by scholars crossing uncharted continents, and by adventurers chasing legends beyond the edge of the known world.

The oldest Ranger Lodges teach that a master Ranger no longer survives because they are stronger than nature, but because they have learned to become part of it. The wilderness no longer feels hostile in their presence; instead, it seems to reveal its secrets willingly. Every rustling leaf, shifting cloud, and distant animal call becomes another piece of a story only the Ranger can truly understand.

Many believe these instincts are supernatural gifts. Rangers simply smile and continue walking, knowing that every lesson was earned through years of hardship, perseverance, and respect for the wild.

---

> *"The wilderness never stops speaking. The greatest Rangers are simply the ones who never stopped listening."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Pathfinder of the Emerald Lodge**

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

entries.title: Weathered Predator
entries.body:
# Weathered Predator

## Overview
The first lesson every Ranger learns is that nature is neither cruel nor kind—it simply exists. Rain will fall, winds will howl, and bitter cold will claim the unprepared. Through countless journeys beneath open skies, the Ranger's body gradually adapts to these everyday hardships, becoming far more resilient than that of an ordinary traveller.

Weathered Predator reflects the beginning of this adaptation. The Ranger no longer dreads travelling through relentless rain or sleeping beneath the stars. Their body naturally resists common weather-related illnesses, allowing them to continue the hunt while others seek warmth and shelter.

Though far from immune to nature's fury, the Ranger has taken the first steps toward becoming one of the wilderness' true survivors.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

The first lesson every Ranger learns is that nature is neither cruel nor kind—it simply exists. Rain will fall, winds will howl, and bitter cold will claim the unprepared. Through countless journeys beneath open skies, the Ranger's body gradually adapts to these everyday hardships, becoming far more resilient than that of an ordinary traveller.

Weathered Predator reflects the beginning of this adaptation. The Ranger no longer dreads travelling through relentless rain or sleeping beneath the stars. Their body naturally resists common weather-related illnesses, allowing them to continue the hunt while others seek warmth and shelter.

Though far from immune to nature's fury, the Ranger has taken the first steps toward becoming one of the wilderness' true survivors.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on saving throws against contracting **weather-related illnesses**, including:
  - Common Cold.
  - Influenza (Flu).
  - Similar non-magical illnesses caused by prolonged exposure to rain, damp conditions, or changing weather.
- Reduce penalties caused by **heavy rain** by **50%**, including penalties to travel, perception, or ranged attacks where appropriate (GM discretion).
- Double the time you can comfortably remain in wet weather before making checks against exposure.
- Gain **+2** to Survival checks made during rainfall or storms.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, apprentices are rarely given comfortable lodgings. Instead, they are encouraged to experience the wilderness in all its forms—walking through days of relentless rain, sleeping beneath soaked cloaks, and learning that discomfort is simply another part of the journey.

Veteran Rangers often joke that they stopped noticing the rain years ago. What once felt cold and miserable has become little more than another companion upon the trail. This quiet resilience is the first step towards enduring the far greater trials that await in Asteria's wild places.

---

> *"Rain only bothers those who still believe they'll stay dry."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's body continues to adapt to the harsh realities of the wilderness. Long days spent traversing frozen trails, enduring relentless snowfall, and surviving bitter mountain nights have hardened both body and mind. Conditions that force most travellers to seek shelter become little more than another challenge to overcome.

While snow and freezing temperatures remain dangerous, the Ranger has learned how to conserve body heat, recognise the earliest signs of exposure, and keep moving when others would falter. This resilience allows them to remain effective during hunts, even when winter itself becomes an enemy.

Among the Ranger Lodges, mastering the frozen wilderness is considered the first true test of a hunter's endurance.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on saving throws against **Hypothermia**, **Frostbite**, and other non-magical cold-weather conditions.
- Reduce penalties caused by **snowfall** and **freezing temperatures** by **50%**, including penalties to travel, perception, and ranged attacks where appropriate (GM discretion).
- Double the amount of time you can safely remain in freezing environments before making Constitution or Endurance checks for exposure.
- Gain **+2** to **Survival** checks made in snowy or frozen environments.
- Ignore movement penalties caused by **light snow** and **shallow snow** outside of combat.

---

### Lore

Every Ranger remembers their first true winter. Endless snow, freezing winds, and bitter nights teach lessons that cannot be learned anywhere else. Those who endure emerge with a newfound respect for the cold, understanding that preparation and perseverance matter far more than strength alone.

Veteran Rangers often travel through snowstorms with little concern, reading tracks hidden beneath fresh snowfall and navigating blizzards by instinct. To them, winter is no longer an obstacle—it is simply another season in which the hunt continues.

Within the Ranger Lodges, surviving the frozen wilds marks the transition from apprentice to seasoned hunter, proving that the wilderness cannot easily claim those who have learned to respect it.

---

> *"Winter does not care how strong you are. It only asks how long you can endure."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

Having conquered the relentless cold, the Ranger now learns to endure the opposite extreme. Scorching deserts, blazing grasslands, volcanic plains, and relentless summer heat are no longer insurmountable obstacles. Through experience and discipline, the Ranger has learned to regulate their body, conserve precious water, and recognise the warning signs of heat exhaustion long before they become life-threatening.

Every expedition across sun-scorched landscapes teaches another lesson in survival. The Ranger instinctively seeks shade, travels with the rhythm of the environment, and understands that patience is often more valuable than speed. What would cripple an inexperienced traveller becomes another challenge to overcome.

Within the Ranger Lodges, surviving both the frozen north and the burning south is considered proof that a hunter has begun to master every face of the wilderness.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on saving throws against **Heat Exhaustion**, **Heatstroke**, **Dehydration**, and other non-magical heat-related conditions.
- Reduce penalties caused by **extreme heat** and **desert environments** by **50%**, including penalties to travel, perception, and ranged attacks where appropriate (GM discretion).
- Double the amount of time you can safely travel in extreme heat before making Constitution or Endurance checks for exposure.
- Consume **50% less water** while travelling through hot or arid environments.
- Gain **+2** to **Survival** checks made in deserts, badlands, volcanic regions, and other hot environments.

---

### Lore

The deserts of Asteria have claimed more lives than many wars. Endless dunes, shimmering heat, and a complete absence of water quickly humble those who underestimate them. Rangers who survive these harsh lands develop an understanding of the sun that few others ever achieve, learning to work with the environment rather than against it.

Among experienced Rangers, it is often said that true endurance is measured not by how long one can march, but by how well one adapts when the world itself becomes the enemy. Those who master the burning wilderness are respected throughout the Lodges, for they have proven that no climate alone can halt the hunt.

---

> *"The desert offers no mercy. It simply rewards those wise enough to respect it."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

By the fourth rank, the Ranger has endured nearly every climate Asteria can offer. They have crossed frozen mountain passes during blizzards, survived weeks beneath relentless desert suns, navigated torrential monsoons, and hunted through violent storms that would force entire caravans to seek shelter.

The Ranger's body and instincts have adapted to nature's most violent expressions. While ordinary travellers struggle against the elements, the Ranger remains focused on the hunt, treating extreme weather as another obstacle to overcome rather than a reason to turn back.

Within the Ranger Lodges, those who reach this level are known as **Stormwalkers**, hunters whose determination is said to rival the fury of nature itself.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on saving throws against all **non-magical weather-related conditions**, including:
  - Hypothermia.
  - Frostbite.
  - Heat Exhaustion.
  - Heatstroke.
  - Dehydration.
  - Weather-related illnesses.
- Reduce penalties caused by **blizzards**, **sandstorms**, **torrential rain**, **high winds**, and similar non-magical weather events by **50%**.
- Gain **+4** to **Survival** checks made during severe weather.
- Double the amount of time you can safely travel through extreme weather before making Constitution or Endurance checks for exposure.
- Natural weather no longer imposes penalties on your ranged weapon attacks unless visibility is completely obscured.
- Ignore movement penalties caused by **deep snow**, **loose sand**, and **heavy mud** outside of combat.

---

### Lore

Only the most accomplished Rangers earn the title of Stormwalker. These hunters have faced nature at its most unforgiving and emerged stronger for it. Their stories tell of tracking prey through raging blizzards, crossing deserts during sandstorms, and pursuing monsters through storms that shattered entire forests.

The Ranger Lodges teach that nature is never an enemy to be conquered, but a force to be understood. Those who survive its greatest trials learn to move with the storm instead of against it. To witness a Stormwalker calmly continue the hunt while lightning tears across the sky is to understand why they are respected throughout Asteria.

---

> *"Most flee when the storm arrives. A Ranger knows the storm often hides the perfect opportunity to hunt."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has become a true master of the wilderness. Years of enduring nature's harshest trials have forged a body and mind capable of thriving where others merely survive. Rain no longer soaks their resolve, freezing winds fail to slow their stride, and blistering deserts cannot break their determination. The wilderness has become their home.

Every environment tells a story, and the Ranger has lived them all. They understand when to move, when to rest, and how to adapt before nature's fury can take its toll. Companions often find themselves surviving impossible journeys simply because they chose to follow a Ranger who has mastered the wild.

Among the Ranger Lodges, those who achieve this rank are honoured as **Wardens of the Wild**, individuals whose knowledge and endurance are considered the pinnacle of mortal survival.

---

### Effects

- Gain **Advantage** on all saving throws against **non-magical environmental effects**, including:
  - Weather-related illnesses.
  - Hypothermia.
  - Frostbite.
  - Heat Exhaustion.
  - Heatstroke.
  - Dehydration.
  - Altitude sickness.
  - Fatigue caused by natural climates.
- Ignore **all penalties** caused by **non-magical weather**, including:
  - Heavy rain.
  - Snowfall.
  - Blizzards.
  - Sandstorms.
  - High winds.
  - Extreme heat.
  - Extreme cold.
- Gain **+6** to all **Survival** checks made in natural environments.
- You require only **half the normal food and water** needed to survive while travelling through natural environments.
- Natural weather never imposes penalties on your ranged weapon attacks or vision unless visibility is completely obscured.
- You automatically succeed on checks to establish a safe campsite or shelter in natural environments, provided suitable materials are available.
- You may travel for **twice as long** in non-magical extreme environments before making Constitution or Endurance checks for fatigue or exposure.

---

### Lore

The title **Warden of the Wild** is rarely bestowed, for it represents the highest expression of a Ranger's relationship with nature. These legendary hunters are spoken of in stories as though they belong to the wilderness itself. They cross frozen tundras without complaint, traverse endless deserts with little more than a waterskin, and emerge from storms that leave entire expeditions stranded.

The Ranger Lodges teach that this mastery is not achieved by conquering nature, but by respecting it. Every storm endured, every mountain crossed, and every frozen night survived becomes another lesson carried for life. Those who reach this level no longer fight against the wilderness—they move with it, understanding its rhythms as naturally as their own heartbeat.

To many, such resilience appears supernatural. Rangers simply smile, knowing that every lesson was earned one difficult journey at a time.

---

> *"Nature does not grant favour to the strongest. It rewards those who learn to endure every season beneath its endless sky."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, Warden of the Emerald Lodge**

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

## Synergy
Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.

entries.title: Hunter's Arsenal
entries.body:
# Hunter's Arsenal

## Overview
A seasoned Ranger understands that every hunt eventually becomes unpredictable. A carefully aimed shot may suddenly become a desperate struggle at arm's length, forcing the hunter to adapt without hesitation. Rather than specialising in a single weapon, Rangers train relentlessly with the tools they carry, ensuring they remain deadly whether their quarry is hundreds of metres away or standing directly before them.

Hunter's Arsenal represents the beginning of this mastery. The Ranger develops the confidence and discipline to fight effectively at any distance, refusing to let close-quarters combat become a weakness. Every weapon carried serves a purpose, and every encounter becomes another opportunity to prove that a true hunter is never caught unprepared.

---

## Rank 1
### Description

A seasoned Ranger understands that every hunt eventually becomes unpredictable. A carefully aimed shot may suddenly become a desperate struggle at arm's length, forcing the hunter to adapt without hesitation. Rather than specialising in a single weapon, Rangers train relentlessly with the tools they carry, ensuring they remain deadly whether their quarry is hundreds of metres away or standing directly before them.

Hunter's Arsenal represents the beginning of this mastery. The Ranger develops the confidence and discipline to fight effectively at any distance, refusing to let close-quarters combat become a weakness. Every weapon carried serves a purpose, and every encounter becomes another opportunity to prove that a true hunter is never caught unprepared.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+2 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-2 penalty to their attack roll**.

---

### Lore

Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices quickly discover that the wilderness rarely allows the perfect engagement. A wounded beast may charge unexpectedly, an ambush may force combat into narrow passages, or an enemy may close the distance before another arrow can be loosed. Those who survive learn to trust every weapon at their side.

Veteran Rangers move confidently between melee and ranged combat without hesitation, understanding that versatility is one of a hunter's greatest strengths. To them, victory does not belong to the weapon—it belongs to the one who knows exactly when to use it.

---

> *"The prey decides the distance. The hunter decides how the fight ends."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 2
### Description

The Ranger's weapon mastery continues to evolve until changing between bow and blade becomes effortless. Every movement has been refined through countless hunts, allowing the Ranger to adapt instantly as enemies close the distance or attempt to retreat. Rather than interrupting the flow of combat, each weapon naturally complements the next.

At this stage, the Ranger no longer thinks about switching weapons—it simply happens. A bow is lowered as a blade is drawn, a spear is cast aside as an axe is gripped, and every transition maintains the relentless momentum of the hunt. Regardless of range, the Ranger always has the right weapon ready.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+3 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-3 penalty to their attack roll**.
- **Once per turn**, you may **draw, sheathe, or swap between a ranged weapon and a hunting weapon** without spending an **Action** or **Action Point**.

---

### Lore

Experienced Rangers know that hesitation is often the difference between a successful hunt and becoming the hunted. Within the Ranger Lodges, apprentices spend years practising weapon transitions until every movement becomes instinctive. The goal is not speed alone, but seamless adaptation to an ever-changing battlefield.

Veteran hunters often appear to carry only a single weapon until the moment combat changes. In one fluid motion, a bow gives way to a blade, or a spear is replaced by an axe, all without breaking stride. To those watching, it seems effortless. To the Ranger, it is simply another lesson learned from the wilderness.

---

> *"The greatest weapon is the one already in your hand when the moment demands it."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 3
### Description

The Ranger has mastered the seamless transition between ranged and melee combat. Every weapon is an extension of the same fighting style, allowing them to respond instinctively as the battlefield shifts around them. Whether striking with a blade before creating distance or firing an arrow at point-blank range, the Ranger wastes neither movement nor opportunity.

Experienced Rangers understand that versatility is their greatest weapon. They no longer think in terms of melee or ranged combat; instead, they simply choose the right tool for the next moment of the hunt. Their fluidity allows them to pressure enemies relentlessly, denying them the chance to exploit distance as a weakness.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+4 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-4 penalty** to their attack rolls.
- **Once per turn**, you may **draw, sheathe, or swap** between a ranged weapon and a hunting weapon without spending an **Action** or **Action Point**.
- **After making a melee attack with a hunting weapon, you may move up to 2 metres without provoking an Opportunity Attack from the creature you attacked.**

---

### Lore

Only veteran Rangers reach the point where weapon changes become almost impossible to perceive. Their movements are smooth and uninterrupted, flowing naturally from bow to blade and back again as though every weapon were crafted as part of the same whole.

Within the Ranger Lodges, this level of mastery is considered a defining trait of a true hunter. Apprentices often spend years attempting to imitate these fluid transitions, only to realise that such precision comes not from speed alone, but from absolute confidence in every weapon they carry.

---

> *"Distance is an illusion. A true hunter is always fighting where they are strongest."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 4
### Description

The Ranger has become a master of adaptive combat, effortlessly transitioning between ranged and melee engagements without sacrificing speed or precision. Every weapon carried serves a purpose, and every movement is calculated to keep the Ranger one step ahead of their opponent. Whether striking from afar or fighting face-to-face, the Ranger maintains complete control over the flow of battle.

At this level, the distinction between ranged and melee combat begins to disappear. The Ranger instinctively knows when to create distance, when to close the gap, and how to seamlessly combine both fighting styles into a relentless assault that keeps enemies constantly reacting.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+5 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-5 penalty** to their attack rolls.
- **Once per turn**, you may **draw, sheathe, or swap** between a ranged weapon and a hunting weapon without spending an **Action** or **Action Point**.
- **After hitting a creature with a hunting weapon**, you may immediately make **one ranged weapon attack** against the same target, provided your ranged weapon is loaded or ready. This attack is made as part of the same Action and may occur only **once per turn**.
- **After making the ranged attack**, you may move **up to 3 metres** without provoking an Opportunity Attack from that creature.

---

### Lore

Among the Ranger Lodges, mastery of Hunter's Arsenal is considered the point where a hunter truly becomes unpredictable. Enemies expecting a drawn-out melee suddenly find themselves struck by an arrow at point-blank range, while those attempting to keep their distance are quickly met with flashing steel.

Veteran Rangers often describe combat as a flowing current rather than a series of isolated attacks. Every movement leads naturally into the next, allowing them to dictate the pace of battle while forcing their quarry to constantly adapt. Those fortunate enough to witness this level of mastery often struggle to identify where one attack ended and the next began.

---

> *"The greatest hunters never choose between bow and blade. They let the hunt decide."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood**

## Rank 5
### Description

The Ranger has achieved complete mastery over every weapon carried into the hunt. To them, bows, blades, spears, and axes are no longer separate disciplines but parts of a single, fluid fighting style. Every movement is deliberate, every transition seamless, allowing the Ranger to adapt instantly to changing threats without ever losing momentum.

Whether an enemy charges into melee or attempts to flee beyond bowshot, the Ranger is always prepared. Their combat style becomes impossible to predict as they flow effortlessly between close-quarters combat and ranged precision. Few opponents survive long enough to exploit a weakness, for the Ranger no longer has one.

Within the Ranger Lodges, only the greatest Huntmasters are said to possess such mastery. They are regarded as warriors capable of defeating their prey regardless of the battlefield, the terrain, or the distance separating hunter and quarry.

---

### Effects

- You **no longer suffer Disadvantage** when making **ranged weapon attacks** against creatures within your melee range.
- Gain a **+6 bonus to attack rolls** when wielding the following hunting weapons:
  - Daggers.
  - Hatchets and Hand Axes.
  - Short Swords.
  - Spears.
  - Other hunting weapons approved by the GM.
- While wielding a ranged weapon, creatures making **Opportunity Attacks** against you suffer a **-6 penalty** to their attack rolls.
- **Once per turn**, you may **draw, sheathe, or swap** between a ranged weapon and a hunting weapon without spending an **Action** or **Action Point**.
- **Once per turn**, after successfully hitting with a **melee attack**, you may immediately make **one ranged weapon attack** against the same creature, provided your ranged weapon is loaded or otherwise ready.
- **Once per turn**, after successfully hitting with a **ranged weapon attack**, you may immediately make **one melee attack** against the same creature if it is within your melee reach.
- After resolving either combination, you may immediately move **up to 3 metres** without provoking an **Opportunity Attack** from that creature.

---

### Lore

The fifth rank of Hunter's Arsenal is considered the pinnacle of martial versatility within the Ranger Lodges. Those who achieve it no longer think in terms of melee or ranged combat. Every weapon becomes part of the same rhythm, each strike naturally flowing into the next as though the hunt itself guides their movements.

Stories tell of legendary Huntmasters who felled charging beasts with an arrow before finishing them with a blade in the same heartbeat, or who cut down a foe in melee before drawing their bow to strike another across the battlefield. Whether embellished or not, these tales all share one truth: a master Ranger is never limited by the weapon in their hands.

---

> *"The weapon does not make the hunter. The hunter makes every weapon worthy of the hunt."*  
> — **Grand Ranger Elyas Thornwood, First Huntmaster of the Emerald Lodge**

## Prerequisites
None

## Scaling
See individual rank details.

Information coming soon.

## GM Notes
GM-only information coming soon.
